sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *el hecho de que* from B2 Unit 6: you start a sentence with a fact that both people already know and then comment on it, so the verb after *que* is in the subjunctive. The 2008 constitution and the rights of nature are full of such facts that people comment on.

sections.title: At work on the topic
rows: El hecho de que la naturaleza tenga derechos es nuevo para muchos países.
present subjunctive: *tenga*; the comment agrees with *el hecho* (singular)
El hecho de que el pueblo aprobara el texto le dio apoyo.
imperfect subjunctive after a past comment: *aprobara*
El hecho de que los jueces hayan aceptado el caso es importante.
El hecho de que un río tenga derechos no significa que nadie pueda usarlo.
*no significa que* + subjunctive, as in B2 Unit 6

items.spanish: El hecho de que la naturaleza tenga derechos es una idea de la Constitución de 2008.
items.english: The fact that nature has rights is an idea of the 2008 constitution.

items.spanish: El hecho de que el pueblo aprobara el texto en un referéndum fue importante.
items.english: The fact that the people approved the text in a referendum was important.

items.spanish: El hecho de que los jueces hayan aceptado el caso es importante para los defensores del bosque.
items.english: The fact that the judges have accepted the case is important for the defenders of the forest.

items.spanish: El hecho de que un río tenga derechos no significa que nadie pueda usarlo.
items.english: The fact that a river has rights does not mean that nobody can use it.

sections.content: Always write *el hecho de que*, with *de*. The comment agrees with *el hecho*, so it is singular: *es importante*, not *son importantes*.
